Light Fall is an inconspicuous platformer at first glance, but it's worth paying attention to.
What really surprises in the first place is the interesting story. Even though it is told using almost static images with simple (but nice) art. Over time, it somehow got under my skin. The voice of the last great owl, Stryx, accompanies you through everything. He is excellently dubbed and his fairy-tale voice will resonate with you. Your hero Nox (I think the game never spells his name) is trying to save his world called Numbra. She is teetering on the brink of extinction, the gods are nowhere to be found, and it is this little hero who will try to save her. As the levels progress, you uncover secrets in short image sequences. The mystery of the vanished gods and also what is happening to the world.

What you would be looking for in the game in vain is some kind of bigger fight. Although you have the option to do some kind of attack with the Shadow Core, its use is primarily for solving puzzles and only lastly for combat. You won't find many real moving enemies here. It is limited to fish jumping out of the surface or crows flying out of corners.

In the game, you have to solve puzzles, because as much as the game is about speed, accuracy and your skill, it is also about cleverness and wit.

So, in my opinion, Light Fall is a great thing for fans of hardcore platformers. If it weren't for the two missteps in the difficulty at the end of the game and the stupid boss fight, I would have aimed the rating higher. [b] 25% [/b]

PHOTOSENSITIVITY WARNING. Part of the game involves being blinded by a repetitive flashing light. There is no warning for this in-game. If you are at all sensitive to light I highly recommend not playing this game.

I mostly enjoyed Light Fall, however I can't recommend it. The game started out great, giving just enough feedback to let the player know what to do but not overwhelm them, slowly ramping up the difficulty. Controls were responsive, aside from some issues with how the character acts on walls. Other than that everything was going really well. Until Act IV. The timing in Act IV is way too tight compared to the rest of the game. You mess up even once and its pretty much over. Even just a half-second of leeway would have made it much better. I'm fine with difficult platformers IF they are difficult throughout or have a decent difficulty ramp. Straight up slapping the player in the face with an seemingly insane difficulty spike is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. I get that the game is geared towards speedrunners, with options in game to help out with that. But it shouldn't hinder the average players enjoyment.

Pros: 
Movement is fluid.
Simple color palette and aesthetic.
Responsive Controls.

Cons:
small part of the game involves being blinded by a repetitive flashing light in the middle of the game with no Photosensitivity Warning anywhere in game. 
Act IV ramps up difficulty quickly taking the game from relatively easy to frustratingly hard.
Timing on Final Boss is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.
Character sometimes likes to cling to walls for dear life, other times struggles to even keep traction.
Simple color palette leads to some foreground and background elements blending together making it hard to see.

This game is pretty and promise a lot of things.
We see what this game has to offer. It pushed us to give our best and try again to succeed and test our determination.
But this game isn't without flaws and it's sad to arrive at the end and feeling unsatisfied.

1. The rooms are big, but the parkour feels very minimalistic at some points. Vipera's forest and the last level seems to be the only levels "charged" with traps and obstacles.

2. Some jumps are really precise and challenging, and are really fun to do. The system of trial and errors is not a bad thing, but at some point it's impossible to not feel frustrated because one spike/deadly crystal killed us at 1 pixel close. After trying to master the moves and do all the jumps correctly, it feels too punishing.

3. The first and last "Bosses" are hard and challenging. The middle one only took us one minute to beat, it was very weird.

4. The controls are original and we loved using all Nox's abilities to progress despite some inconsistencies.

5. Sometimes you are stuck into walls, and it's pretty infuriating because it breaks your momentum, especially during the last boss fight. They could have added a button to cling to walls instead.

6. Only 2 collectibles, for only 2 achievements, not even a secret cutscene to reward you for saving everyone and reading all Paddlewood fanfic chapters.

7. And the most disapointing part, the story. It's linear, flat, unsurprising. The game is so nervous you never take the time to bond with the main characters. You don't feel concerned by what's happening. The lore is slammed into your face and you can't even digest it that you are teleported to the next level. You can even skip the cutscenes showing how the story wasn't the main point of the game. They tried to make a rich story, but there are so much elements the lore tells but never show you. The dragon, the big anaconda, the giant worm? Forget them, you will never have Paddlewood's chance to meet them.
(At some point, Paddlewood seems to have a more interesting adventure than us).
The animation is pretty and the character design is very cute, but except the owl, the villain and the gods, no other npc's. Even the villagers you saved are conveniently hidden behind the camera for the 3 seconds the cutscene show them free.
And the ending of course is a succession of cliches and even if the main villain (that you encounter only at the very end) has ONE interesting sentence about how we are MAYBE to blame about what happened, it's never questioned after. Luxanna sacrifies herself and we don't know what happened to the vilain army, as if they never existed.

In conclusion, the game has a huge potential, and it tries very hard. But it's obviously a game only made for speedrunners and people who want to master all the skills and levels, not for people who are interested in discovering the lore by themselves.
It's not a "bad" game, but it feels incomplete, or it tried to to propose to many things at the same time and at the end it feels like a blurry mess.
Buy this game if you are interested in speedy levels, the game is clearly made for speedruns only.
But buy it with at least 30% of reduction, because it's not a game you can spend hundreds of hours on it.

I’ll be honest,
I like unique Platformers, i feel they get a bad rap and when i find one with an interesting world, mechanics, story, or controls that feel good to play I get excited!. 

This game looks pretty good, the art looks nice and the game seems to have something going for it. 

but the cons from playing for even a bit severely outway the pros. i normally don’t review games with so little time on them, but i feel as though i have had enough and even introducing new mechanics and story beats won’t change much due to:

1. Poor and Unsatisfying controls:
the game itself can look as pretty as it can but the controls feel bad, there is some good game feel when you run for example but i had a hard time precisely controlling my character. i died so many times and had a pretty bad time just moving my character.


2. A Bland Story & World
This is probably the most subjective category and i have not completed the game so take this section as an early impression. I am usually either a gameplay control guy or narrative guy, (meaning i either play games that control well or games with good narratives\worlds), i tried to get into the story but a world ravaged by something just wasn’t incentive enough for me to care. i don’t know who i am playing nor am i given a reason to care. give me a reason to go on this adventure and people who i can care about.

3. Bad Art Direction
this is massive sadly.
the art is gorgeous and the animations are amazing.
but the color direction is not just bad, it actively hurts gameplay. there is sometimes 1 color for both the platforms and the background making it difficult to see what i can do.


Conclusion:
Bishop Games gave it their best shot, and despite producing a beautiful game, have failed by creating one with unresponsive and floaty controls, a dull and generic world that makes me feel no need to explore it, poor art direction that causes difficulty to actually play the game, and an innovative game mechanic that is severly hampered by all of the above.

Bishop games, if you are by chance reading this. i am sorry for the harsh words. i feel you guys, and i hope you take this opportunity to learn, see what you can do better, why things didn’t work out, there is something interesting here, but it’s muddled down the design, both art, narrative, and game. i honestly believe you have the skills of making a great game, usually, people are great at designing the games they love to play. if you ever do make a new game and need a playtester, i promise to be 100% honest with you.

This game is a lot of fun 95% of the time. The entire game is pretty free to let you explore at your own pace, but the last level is all outrunning various things and the pace is something the game never prepares you for. The last level is just frustrating and takes forever to finish as you keep repeating each little race over and over again. Aside from that issue, the rest of the game is a lot of fun. The mechanics are interesting and it's fun to control your little shadow guy around the map. I had a few instances where the game didn't seem to accept my button inputs. I haven't had that issue with this controller anywhere else, so I know it isn't my controller. 

The whole point of this game is the platforming and the atmosphere. Those are both great. The rest of the game is just kind of there. The music is fine, but nothing special, but it isn't insulting or anything either. The plot is kind of there. Things keep getting accomplished as you play through, though you never really fight anyone, it's just more platforming so I'm not really sure how we actually "defeat" the villain of the game, but it doesn't really bother me here. Sometimes it can be difficult to figure out which parts of the map are background and which I can interact with. I even managed to clip into the wall at one point and then couldn't get out.

Overall, it's fun to play, minus the final level, but it's all about the platforming. Don't expect anything else besides the gameplay.

TLDR: Definitely recommend the game for platforming fans; great gameplay and dedicated speedrun mode, the game devs actually listen to the community, and beautiful artwork. If you're not going to try to 100% or speedrun the game, though, I'd suggest waiting for it to go on sale.

Overall, Light Fall is the type of game you'd expect if you looked at it before you played it - a 2D platformer. The soundtrack is good, but nothing too special; the art is actually pretty amazing; and it has tight, intuitive gameplay (ever notice that the box moves with you for a bit if you summon it while running? It's a critical - but easy to miss - detail that keeps the gameplay fun). Now, personally I felt like the story was a bit lackluster - it had a few cliches thrown in - but it wasn't so awful or nonsensical that it detracted from the game. Normally, I don't write reviews. However, there was one thing that used to bug me SO much that they fixed, and that warranted a review. The final boss used to be a huge issue for me - you used to have to stand around waiting for some stupid amounts of time for it to start up its next attack, its attacks were super easy to avoid if you just memorized the patterns (some were even so dumb that you could use your boxes to climb over the attack completely). Overall, it just felt like a waiting game, and eventually I just gave up the game because I didn't want to have to fight that boss again in speedrun mode. However, Bishop Games took a risk that few games are ever willing to take - they completely reworked the final boss. What an undertaking this must have been! Seeing the change, I decided to give the new boss a try. It was incredible! Instead of waiting around forever, the boss is now high-intensity platforming. Now, instead of the boss constantly throwing the same voice lines at you over and over ad nauseum, it goes through all of its voice lines once and then shuts up. Instead of waiting forever for a chance to get one hit (of three) in, you now get to hit him once after completing the platforming sections (and you only have to hit him once). What a change! That's a significant amount of reprogramming and redesigning to do; additionally, despite the rather small fanbase for this game, Bishop has been releasing patches and bugfixes for the game to improve the quality of life since release. For example, they recently added "Inverted Sprint," where instead of holding the button to sprint, you can map that button as "walk" instead and have sprint set as your default state. These changes show what sets this game apart from other games you might see - the game devs actually listen to and care about what the fanbase says! Overall, the gameplay is the most important aspect of a platformer - and this game nails it. 

8.2/10, game devs listen

I don't know wheter to recommend Light Fall or not. I enjoyed the game and hope to continue doing so as a speed game, because that's really what this game was designed as. It isn't meant to be a difficult experience, but rather a repeatable one. It's a good racing game, not something you should look toward for a large amount of content, for that is my biggest gripe about Light Fall. My final verdict is at the end.

[h1] Story Mode - My thoughts and what should be expected from a casual playthrough [/h1]
I finished the Story Mode in about 4 hours. At the beginning I wasn't impressed with the story. [spoiler]You wake up alone and lost while a mysterious owl talks about you.[/spoiler] It leaves you in the dark for the first Act. At the beginning of the second act, more gets revealed and ramps up becomming very interesting and I found myself satisfied at the end.

[h1] An Incredible Platforming Mechanic [/h1]
The game's main mechanic revolves around the protagonist's Shadow Core, a magic box that can be used in several different ways, most importantly to create a surface that can be climbed or ran on. I was really impressed by how the physics engine and the shadow core used momentum, with the exception of [spoiler]the boosts in 4-4[/spoiler]. It felt nice to use, espically as the story progressed and it had some significance.

The climbing on walls and steep slopes was intersting and is something i am not impressed with. There is little friction or ability to hang on walls. You have to keep jumping or simply fall.

[h1]Replayability and Speedrun Mode[/h1]

I have been speedrunning since Janurary of 2018. [url=https://www.speedrun.com/user/yote]Here is my page on speedrun.com for those who are interested.[/url] I've ran several games, both good and bad speed games. [b]As far as I know[/b], there is no RNG, or random elements for those who aren't familiar with speedrunning terms. Light Fall is an excellent way to start speedrunning. It is integreated into the game and even has its own seperate mode to save your ESC key trying to skip all the cutscenes. I've noticed nothing wrong with the in-game timer. The game is replayable and still has plenty of room for optimization on the [url=https://www.speedrun.com/Light_Fall]Official Speedrun.com Leaderboard[/url].

[h1] Community [/h1]

I've never seen a community this amazing and so friendly. I've experienced very toxic Rainbow 6 Siege and CS:GO communities for several years, and I've experienced nice speedrunning communities, but damn, I've never seen a group of people this nice and developers so open to their community. Seriously, the Bishop Games team is amazing. I highly recommend you go join [url=http://discord.gg/lightfall]The Official Light Fall Discord[/url]. You should be greated with warm welcomes from the community.

[h1] Final Verdict [/h1]

As a casual I would not recommend this game at full price. If you can catch a good sale however, I'd say it is very much worth it. If you look at this game as a good speed game and are determined to stick with it and submit times, I would highly recommend it. The community and core gameplay is great, while the story and other artistic aspects are also very good. I don't know what I'd rate this game out of 100, but I'd suggest between 70 and 95. The game is great, but has it's major flaw: the lack of content for casual players.

I appriciate you reading this review and I hope I helped you decide whether or not to purchase Light Fall. Regardless, I suggest you hang out in the [url=http://discord.gg/lightfall]Light Fall Discord[/url]

Overall I quite enjoyed Light Fall, though I'm not fully done with it yet (I have yet to finish my Hard mode playthrough, and there are still some of the gameplay challenges left to go), but there were a few things I disliked.

First and foremost, the length of the game was definitely a bit frustrating. I have a significant amount of experience in platformers (I have 275 hours in Super Meat Boy, and 60 hours in Celeste, both of which are significantly more difficult near the end than this game was), and that unfortunately meant that this game was pretty short. Had I not taken a break after finishing 2/3rds of the final level and having to redo it, I would have finished the game in just under 3 hours. There is definitely more gameplay after the main story, as I didn't do Hard mode, nor the gameplay challenges listed in the achievements, nor did I spend a lot of time scouring for all the collectibles (which took me about an hour and a half to two hours to go back and finish on a second sweep).

That said, the game was definitely enjoyable. The gameplay reminded me heavily of Super Meat Boy - while this is generally a good thing, it does have the issue of needing to hold down the right trigger button almost constantly, which is a strain if you're not used to it. There were a few issues here, with overlap between walljumping and placing a block and so on, but for the most part they were uncommon and didn't interfere with normal play. The art and sound/music are wonderful. I wasn't really a fan of the narrator's voice, but it was certainly tolerable. 

Overall, I would recommend the game on a decent sale if you're someone with significant experience in platformers like myself, and for someone who was new to the genre this would definitely be a great place to start even at full price.
